messages:
sam (AE): Heads-up — Prospect (Zenith Health) POC streaming failing on mobile. They report SSE lines arriving incomplete, client JSON parse errors, and frequent disconnects. CC @maria (SE).

maria (SE): Thanks Sam. Short checklist: client SDK version, network type (wifi/cell), any proxies or MDM, and a quick log snippet.

kai (iOS): Repro on iPhone 13 and iPhone SE. SDK 1.4.0. Happening on home wifi and on LTE. Stack: `NSStreamErrorDomain: -1005 (Network connection lost)` then JSON decode error about unexpected EOF.

maria (SE): Ok that pattern points to abrupt connection reset rather than server closing cleanly. Two streams of work: server keepalive + disable proxy buffering; client resilience (reconnect + incremental parser).

tess (eng): We can enable comment-style keepalive every 10s (SSE `: keepalive

`) and set `X-Accel-Buffering: no` on the POC nginx route so responses flush quickly. Also confirmed our ingress sent `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` and `Content-Type: text/event-stream`.

ops-bot: server-log 1798130051: conn_close reason=client_reset dur=9.8s peer=18.205.33.10 route=/v1/stream?sse=1 status=200 bytes_sent=4120

maria (SE): Ops shows client reset after ~10s which matches the mobile traces. Likely: mobile OS or carrier reaps idle connection, or app-level read timeout. Two immediate suggestions: (1) client: increase read timeout / disable aggressive keepalives in OS; (2) server: heartbeat + smaller flush intervals.

kai (iOS): Can you confirm whether the server sends newline-terminated event blocks and not huge coalesced payloads? Some mobile parsers choke on very large chunk coalescing.

tess (eng): We flush after every event by default, but certain proxies (ALB, corporate gateways) can buffer. POC route currently through CDN. We can temporarily bypass CDN for the POC to test direct origin. Also we pushed a client library patch yesterday (1.4.1) that improves partial-chunk handling by buffering until a full JSON object is available rather than failing immediately.

kai (iOS): We'll test 1.4.1. For immediate mitigation can the server send a small comment every 8s? That often keeps connections alive on carriers.

maria (SE): Yes, enabling server heartbeat is low risk; ops can toggle it. Also request logs and a pcap if problem persists. If they can't produce pcap, a device-level tcpdump would help.

security: Zenith's security team also asked about private connectivity options since their mobile users go through a corporate MDM that enforces TLS inspection and they won't whitelist many IP ranges. That is a procurement blocker — they are asking about Dedicated + PrivateLink.

sam (AE): Noted — I'll surface Dedicated/PrivateLink options and pricing. That may also remove some CDN buffering and help consistency.

kai (iOS): Quick test results: upgraded to 1.4.1 + extended read timeout, and we asked Redwood to enable heartbeat + bypass CDN for a test route. After 6 hours the reconnects reduced significantly; there was one disconnect during a wifi->cell handoff where OS reset the TCP. On reconnect our client re-established stream and requested missing tokens.

maria (SE): Great. Action items: (1) Client teams to roll 1.4.1 and implement reconnect/resume logic; (2) Ops to keep heartbeat + temporary CDN bypass for the POC window; (3) Sam to follow up on Dedicated/PrivateLink pricing and security Qs; (4) If remaining failures occur, get pcap and device logs for deep dive.

sam (AE): I'll coordinate with Zenith for procurement and ask if they can run a short traffic window for us to collect pcaps. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
